title: The computer's memory is reporting errors
why: Faulty memory can corrupt files and crash programs in ways that are hard to trace.
fix_summary: Back up your files, then test the memory sticks one at a time.
manual: Back up, then restart from the Secure Linux USB stick and run Memtest86+ overnight.

title: The memory test found faulty memory
why: Faulty memory corrupts data. It can damage files without you noticing.
fix_summary: Back up your files, then replace the faulty memory stick.
manual: Replace the memory. Test one stick at a time to find the bad one.

title: The processor reported hardware errors
why: Hardware errors from the processor or memory mean something is physically wrong or overheating.
fix_summary: Back up your files and check cooling.
manual: Back up now. Clean the vents, check the fans, then test the memory.

title: The processor made mistakes when working hard
why: A processor that makes mistakes under load usually means overheating or faulty hardware.
manual: Clean the vents and fans, then test again. If it still fails, get the computer checked.

title: The processor is running too hot
why: Too much heat slows the computer, shortens its life and can shut it off suddenly.
manual: Clean the vents and fans with compressed air, and use the computer on a hard flat surface.

title: The processor is slowing itself down to cool off
why: When the processor gets too warm it slows down to protect itself, so the computer feels sluggish.
manual: Clean the vents and fans, and check the power mode is not stuck on performance.

title: A fan has stopped while the computer is warm
why: A stopped fan lets the computer overheat, which can damage it.
manual: Switch off, let it cool, clean the fan and check it spins. Get it repaired if it does not.

title: Something inside is dangerously hot
why: Parts that get this hot can be damaged, and the computer may shut itself off.
manual: Switch off and let it cool. Clean the vents and fans before using it again.

title: The computer may be clogged with dust
what: It runs at {detail} degrees even though the fans are turning. That often means dust or old heat-paste.
why: Dust blocks air flow, which makes the computer hot, noisy and slow.
manual: Clean the vents with compressed air. If still hot, a shop can replace the heat-paste.

title: The processor's built-in fixes are not installed
what: The package with the processor's latest built-in fixes (microcode) was not found.
why: It carries security and stability fixes from the maker.
fix_summary: Install the processor and hardware drivers that are missing. Needs the internet.
undo: Remove the package with your package manager if needed.
manual: Run: sudo secure-linux-drivers install

title: The processor model has known security weaknesses
why: Some processors have flaws that are only partly fixed by software.
fix_summary: Installing updates and the latest BIOS gives the best protection.
manual: Keep the system updated and install BIOS updates from the maker.

title: One program is using almost all of the processor
why: A program that never stops working makes the computer slow, hot and noisy.
fix_summary: Nothing is closed automatically, because it could be your work.
manual: Open the system monitor, find the program at the top, and close it. Save your work first.

title: One program is using more than half of the memory
why: That program may be stuck or leaking memory, which slows down everything else.
fix_summary: Nothing is closed automatically, because it could be your work.
manual: Open the system monitor, find the program at the top and restart it.

title: The computer has been overloaded for a while
what: It has had far more work than it can handle for the last quarter of an hour.
why: This makes everything slow and the fans loud.
manual: Close big programs or restart. Check the system monitor for what is busy.

title: The computer ran out of memory and closed programs
why: When memory runs out the system closes programs without warning, and you can lose unsaved work.
fix_summary: Nothing changes automatically; closing programs or adding memory helps.
manual: Close programs you do not use, or add more memory.

title: Memory is almost full right now
what: Only {detail}% of memory is free at the moment.
why: The computer slows right down when memory is nearly full.
manual: Close browser tabs and programs you are not using.

title: The battery is wearing out
what: The battery now holds only about {detail}% of what it did when new.
why: A worn battery gives short running time and can swell if left.
manual: Plan a battery replacement. An 80% charge limit slows further wear.

title: The charger is plugged in but the battery is not charging
why: The charger may be too weak, the plug loose, or the battery may be failing.
manual: Try another socket and the original charger. Check the plug is in all the way.

title: The charger is too weak for this computer
why: A weaker charger cannot keep up when the computer is busy, so the battery drains while plugged in.
manual: Use the original charger, or one with the same or more watts.

title: The computer cannot see a charger
what: A battery exists, but no charger input is reported.
why: Some laptops only report power when plugged in.
manual: Check the plug and charger. Try a different socket.

title: The battery is almost empty
what: The battery is down to {detail}% and the charger is not connected.
why: The computer will switch off soon and unsaved work could be lost.
manual: Save your work and plug in the charger.

title: You can make the battery last longer
what: Your laptop can stop charging at 80%, which makes the battery last years longer, but this is not switched on.
why: Charging to 100% all the time wears a battery faster.
fix_summary: Stop charging at 80%. You can charge fully before a trip with one command.
manual: Run: secure-linux-battery limit 80

title: The computer is in performance mode on battery
what: It is running on the battery with the "performance" power mode, which drains it quickly.
why: Balanced mode saves a lot of battery with little difference in speed.
fix_summary: Switch to the balanced power mode.
manual: Choose Balanced in the battery menu.

detector: cmd:jprev~PM: (suspend|hibernate) entry failed|Failed to suspend|Freezing of tasks failed
title: The computer failed to go to sleep
why: A device or driver stopped the computer from sleeping, so the battery can drain in a bag.
manual: Update the system and firmware. If it continues, unplug USB devices before sleeping.
